speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your patience. To begin my assessment of the skin condition on your left dorsal hand, could you describe exactly what you see there, such as its color, texture, and size? Additionally, when did you first notice these changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history; given your age and outdoor activities, has the lesion on your left dorsal hand been changing in size, shape, or color recently? Have you noticed any pain, itching, bleeding, or crusting at the site?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Given your history of sun exposure and the "sandpaper-like" description of the plaque, this is highly consistent with a solar-induced precancerous skin lesion. I will not request further tests as the clinical presentation is classic, but I recommend strict sun protection and a follow-up in six months to monitor for any changes.
